dosageRegimens.notes: Within 30 minutes of bedtime, with at least 7 hours remaining before the planned wake time. Taking with or soon after a large meal delays onset by about 1.3 hours.
Moderate impairment (Child-Pugh 7-9). Not recommended in severe impairment (Child-Pugh 10 or above).

mechanismsOfAction.note: Blocks orexin-A and orexin-B signalling at OX1 and OX2, removing the wake-promoting drive rather than adding a sedative one. Mechanistically distinct from the GABA-A hypnotics in this set, though the practical result stacks with them.

metabolismPathways.note: 89% of metabolic clearance. No other CYP contributes more than 3%. This makes daridorexant exposure almost entirely a function of 3A4 activity, so a 3A4 inhibitor is a dose change in disguise.

activeMetabolites.name: None clinically relevant
activeMetabolites.note: Extensively metabolised, but circulating metabolites do not contribute meaningfully to effect.

pharmacokinetics.notes: Volume of distribution is reported as an absolute 31 L rather than weight-normalised. No accumulation on repeat nightly dosing. Renal impairment, age, sex and body size do not meaningfully change exposure; hepatic impairment does.

interactions.suggestedAction: Separate by as many hours as possible. Taking a stimulant late and then a hypnotic to compensate produces a cycle where each dose justifies the next.
interactions.note: Directly opposing effects on arousal. The stimulant does not shorten the hypnotic's duration, so the combination yields impaired sleep quality plus next-day residual sedation rather than cancelling out.

interactions.suggestedAction: Avoid, or halve the daridorexant dose to 25 mg and do not exceed it. Famotidine is the straightforward substitute.
interactions.note: 89% of daridorexant's metabolic clearance is CYP3A4, so its exposure is close to a direct function of 3A4 activity. Next-morning driving impairment is the dose-related risk the label caps for.

interactionScreening.note: No individually documented pair. Colestipol's general labelling rule applies: give any other oral medication at least 1 hour before, or 4 hours after.

notes: Schedule IV. The 7-hour rule is not a formality: next-morning driving impairment is dose-related and is the reason the label caps at 50 mg.
